seoDescription: The Churchman Lab at Harvard Medical School studies how gene expression is regulated across the cell, from the nucleus to the mitochondria. We build quantitative sequencing methods — NET-seq, nano-COP, subcellular TimeLapse-seq, mtFiber-seq — to measure transcription, RNA processing, RNA flow between compartments, and mitonuclear coordination.

hero.eyebrow: Department of Genetics · Harvard Medical School
hero.title: From the nucleus to mitochondria, we study the many layers of gene regulation.
hero.body: A cell makes thousands of mRNAs every minute and controls every one of them — where it is made, how it is processed, how long it survives, and whether it is ever translated. We build quantitative methods that make those steps measurable, in both the nuclear and the mitochondrial genome.
hero.imageAlt: Single-nucleoid architecture reveals heterogeneous packaging of mitochondrial DNA, a painting by Leidy Churchman
hero.caption: Leidy Churchman, Single-nucleoid architecture reveals heterogeneous packaging of mitochondrial DNA (2024)

recentWork.title: Three things we have learned lately

items.title: Two genomes run on different clocks
items.body: By measuring RNA production, processing, ribosome association and degradation across both genomes, we found that nearly every step runs at a starkly different rate. The mitoribosome acts as a key point of coordination between the two systems.
items.imageAlt: A kinetic dichotomy between mitochondrial and nuclear gene expression processes, a painting by Leidy Churchman

items.title: Single-molecule views of transcription and chromatin
items.body: Long-read chromatin fiber sequencing lets us see RNA polymerases in their native chromatin context along 30 kb fibers, revealing direct coordination and anti-coordination between neighboring genes, enhancers and insulators.

items.title: RNA kinetics from an ordinary RNA-seq library
items.body: AIR-seq marks new RNA with N4-hydroxycytidine, which base-pairs ambiguously and so shows up as mismatches in standard libraries — no chemical conversion, no enrichment. RNA synthesis and decay rates now come out of ordinary bulk and single-cell experiments.

lab.title: Biologists, physicists, chemists and computational scientists working together
lab.body: The lab has always been a mix. Stirling trained as a physicist and the people here now came in through biochemistry, neuroscience, chemistry, and computation.

resources.title: Methods, code and protocols, all publicly available

items.title: GeneWalk
items.body: Identifies which functions of a gene actually matter in your biological context, by learning vector representations of genes and GO terms on a condition-specific network. pip install genewalk.

items.title: Protocols
items.body: Published, benchtop-ready protocols for NET-seq, nano-COP, subcellular RNA-seq and mitoribosome profiling — with the corrections we have issued since publication.

recruitment.title: We are recruiting postdocs and rotation students
recruitment.body: We take people from biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, mathematics and engineering. If you want to answer a question about gene regulation with our novel set of methods--or develop your own--we should talk!
